claims.evidence: The witness noted a sticker on the unit but the text was not legible; the pin count was not observed.
Origin of used parts cannot be determined through visual inspection alone.
No testing status or proof of functionality was shown in the report.
Mileage is not recorded on the gearbox housing.
The report mentions signs of use but does not confirm the state of factory seals or bolts.

risks.risk: Incompatibility with the stated vehicle (wrong model or pin count).
risks.proof: A clear, legible photo of the identification sticker and a close-up of the electrical connector pins.
risks.if_unproven: As a generic, unidentified gearbox for scrap or parts.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical failure or burnt clutch plates.
risks.proof: A video showing the color and smell of the transmission fluid (ATF) and a shot of the input shaft being turned manually.
risks.if_unproven: As a non-functional unit requiring a full rebuild.

risks.risk: Structural damage such as hairline cracks in the bell housing.
risks.proof: High-resolution photos of the entire casing from all angles, specifically the mounting points.
risks.if_unproven: As a damaged core with potential for leaks.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the white sticker on the torque converter/housing.
Close-up photo of the electrical connector showing the 22 pins.
Photo of the transmission fluid drained or on a dipstick (if applicable).
Photos of all sides of the metal housing to check for cracks or welds.
response.reason: The witness could not verify the model, year, or pin count due to an illegible sticker. Without confirmation that this is a 22-pin Camry gearbox, it cannot be priced even at a worst-case for that specific model.
